nodes.label: Supermux iOS app target
nodes.rationale: CFBundleVersion/CFBundleShortVersionString are tracked to the build settings so OTA installs actually supersede each other (XcodeGen otherwise hardcodes CFBundleVersion=1). NSAllowsArbitraryLoads is on because dev builds reach a self-hosted broker over LAN/Tailscale, often plain http.

nodes.label: SupermuxWatch watchOS target
nodes.rationale: Embedded in the iOS app for paired install / TestFlight; needs its own NSAllowsArbitraryLoads or watchOS ATS blocks the ws:// broker connection.

nodes.label: SupermuxPushNSE (Notification Service Extension)
nodes.rationale: Intercepts mutable-content pushes and decrypts the sealed blob on-device. PushCrypto.swift / PushKeypair.swift / PushGroupState.swift are compiled into BOTH the app and the extension, and a shared Keychain access group lets the NSE read the keypair the app generated.

nodes.label: SupermuxNotifContent (Notification Content Extension)
nodes.rationale: Draws the expanded long-press mini-transcript from the notification userInfo the NSE sets — no App Group and no network — and is iOS-only because macOS has no content extensions.

nodes.label: SupermuxMac macOS app target
nodes.rationale: Excludes Watch/** (WatchConnectivity does not exist on macOS), overrides PRODUCT_NAME/PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME to Supermux so @testable import matches, brands the system accent via ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME (AppKit selection ignores SwiftUI .tint), and ships Developer ID + notarization instead of the Mac App Store because native hosting needs an unsandboxed distribution.

nodes.label: SupermuxMacPushNSE (macOS twin of the push NSE)
nodes.rationale: Same principal class and same shared crypto sources as the iOS NSE (CryptoKit is cross-platform); only the platform and entitlements differ.

nodes.label: Kotlin Shared.framework embed-and-sign pre-build phase
nodes.rationale: Runs ./gradlew --no-daemon :shared:embedAndSignAppleFrameworkForXcode: --no-daemon because the embed step calls codesign and a detached Gradle daemon loses the calling session's keychain access (errSecInternalComponent) when signing headlessly over SSH. ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING=NO is required for the phase to reach outside the sandbox.

nodes.label: Post-build phase: sign bundled native host helpers
nodes.rationale: Codesigns supermux-broker, frpc and tmux inside HostResources with --options runtime after the build, guarded on CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED / EXPANDED_CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY so unsigned/simulator builds skip it. Hardened runtime rejects unsigned nested executables.

nodes.label: EditorWeb bundled as a folder reference
nodes.rationale: index.html + cm6.js are added as a folder (not a group) so the directory structure survives into the .app bundle and Bundle.main can resolve them with subdirectory: "EditorWeb" for the WKWebView editor.

nodes.label: SupermuxMacTests (macOS twin test bundle)
nodes.rationale: Excludes WatchSessionStatusTests / RelayEnvelopeTests / BrokerRelayTests / RoutingTransportTests because the Watch-only wire types they exercise are compiled only into the iOS target. TEST_HOST must be overridden because XcodeGen guesses it from the TARGET name (SupermuxMac) while the built product is Supermux.app, otherwise xcodebuild fails with 'Could not find test host'.

nodes.label: SupermuxMacUITests (XCUITest smoke)
nodes.rationale: Drives the built app as a separate host process, so TEST_TARGET_NAME uses the XcodeGen TARGET name (SupermuxMac) — verified empirically — and needs no TEST_HOST-style override because XcodeGen resolves it against the target list itself.

nodes.label: Watch wire-format sources shared into the iOS app
nodes.rationale: RelayEnvelope.swift, BrokerTransport.swift and WatchSessionStatus.swift are compiled into the iOS app as standalone source entries so the phone-side BrokerRelay and SupermuxTests can use the same relay wire format as the watch.

nodes.label: Release-only manual Apple Distribution signing
nodes.rationale: Manual signing is scoped to Release so Debug/simulator builds stay automatic; the SDK-qualified CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY[sdk=iphoneos*] key is required because Xcode's built-in iPhone Developer default otherwise wins. Provisioning profiles are set per app/extension target while SwiftPM deps sign with the identity and take no profile.
